summary: Spartanburg Downtown Memorial Airport (SPA) is a city-owned general aviation facility serving the Spartanburg, South Carolina metropolitan area in the Upstate region. Located just a few miles southwest of downtown Spartanburg, it primarily supports corporate, recreational, and flight training operations rather than scheduled commercial service. The airport provides an important gateway for the regional business community and is well-positioned near major transportation corridors in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
faqs:
Q: Does Spartanburg Downtown Memorial Airport have commercial airline service?
A: No, SPA is a general aviation airport without scheduled commercial flights. The nearest commercial airport is Greenville-Spartanburg International (GSP), located about 20 miles to the west.

Q: What is the airport primarily used for?
A: The airport serves corporate aviation, private pilots, flight training, and recreational flying, and also hosts air shows and community events throughout the year.

Q: Are there FBO services available at SPA?
A: Yes, the airport has fixed-base operator (FBO) facilities providing fuel, hangar space, aircraft maintenance, and other services for general aviation users.

Q: How close is the airport to downtown Spartanburg?
A: The airport is approximately 3 miles southwest of downtown Spartanburg, making it a quick drive from the city center.
transport_tips: Rental cars are the most convenient option for reaching downtown Spartanburg, as the airport is only a short drive away. Rideshare services such as Uber and Lyft operate in the area, and local taxi companies also serve the airport. The airport's proximity to I-85 and I-26 makes it easy to connect to Greenville, Asheville, or Charlotte by ground transport.
local_tip: If you have time to spare, visit the BMW Zentrum visitor center near the Greer exit off I-85, which is about a 30-minute drive from the airport and offers tours of the only BMW manufacturing plant in North America.
